summary: I ASSEMBLED THE REAL LOOP AND DROVE IT WITH THE REAL OPT, and the headline is that opt.build can replace the hand-built AdamW the r2 sweep had to substitute. Sequence, exactly as spine/compose.py::ASSEMBLY_ORDER declares it: DATA.open_areas -> TOK.build_vocabulary -> DATA.data_plan -> DATA.draw_stream -> TOK.tokenize -> LM.resolve -> LM.build_model -> FAB.build -> SIG.build -> OPT.build(param_groups={'base': model.parameters()+Population.parameters(), 'encoder': SIG.encoder_parameters()}, run_windows=Windows(2068)) -> per step LM.encode/LM.decode/cross_entropy -> OPT.scaled_backward -> OPT.maybe_step -> OPT.counters. Harness at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/vopt/harness.py; every arm is a fresh process. 1200 REAL OPTIMIZER STEPS, FRESH BATCH EVERY STEP: cross-entropy 8.3329 -> 2.2485 nats/token (6.6324 -> 1.8264 bits/byte at the measured 1.810 bytes/token), lr tracking the schedule from 1.94e-05 at step 1 up to the 2e-3 peak at the clamped warmup of 206 and back down to 9.49e-04 by step 1200, grad-norm p50 2.06 / p99 6.12, opt.backward=1200 opt.step=1200 and counters()'s accumulation invariant not raising. THE BATCH WAS NOT FIXED (a 16-window slice walked through the stream), but the stream is only 2068 windows so 1200x16 draws is ~9 passes over one 66k-token synthetic corpus and there is no held-out number here -- this is 'the loop descends', not a generalisation result. The fixed-batch arm is reported separately and reaches 0.0085 (overfitting one batch, a smoke test). ACCUM, CLIP, DETERMINISM AND RESUME ALL HOLD, each with numbers, and the accumulation scaling was checked against a true full-batch gradient rather than against a counter. THE FABRIC RESULT IS THE ONE THAT CHANGES SOMETHING. A and B DO move under the real optimizer -- 0.00538 / 0.00554 over 30 steps, 0.1954 / 0.1724 over 1200 -- but ONLY when the loss uses them the way a router would. Under the exact stand-in term .rework/audits/r2_sweep_full.json records, grad(A) and grad(B) are IDENTICALLY ZERO and the real OPT moves A by exactly 0.0. The recorded 0.000529 was not learning: it was torch.optim.AdamW's DEFAULT weight_decay=0.01 shrinking A toward the origin, reproduced to four figures. THREE SIBLING AUDITS (.rework/audits/v_opt_units.json, v_opt_contract.json, v_opt_gates.json, all written 2026-09-03 23:31-23:48) already exist for this package, which my task brief did not know about; where I hit something they filed, I say so and give the runtime evidence rather than re-file it as new.

findings.detail: THE REAL OPT CAN REPLACE THE HAND-BUILT AdamW, WHICH IS THE QUESTION THE TASK ASKS. opt.build accepts the param groups spine/compose.py::_base_parameters actually assembles -- list(model.parameters()) + list(Population.parameters()) as 'base', SIG.encoder_parameters() as 'encoder' -- and constructs both AdamW instances. Measured at the shipped defaults with LM_ARCH=transformer LM_WIDTH=64 LM_CTX=32 LM_LAYERS=2, FAB_N0=8 FAB_SLOTS=16, DATA_SOURCE=synthetic DATA_AREAS=eng,py: vocab 512 ids at 1.8112 bytes/token, 66204 tokens -> 2068 windows, 48 base tensors (28 model + 20 fabric) and 3 encoder tensors, group_overlap=0. Horizon(run_steps=Steps(2068), warmup=Steps(206), wavelength=Steps(2068), n_cycles=1); opt.build.warmup_asked=1000 opt.build.warmup=206 opt.build.warmup_clamped=1, i.e. the run_steps//10 clamp fired and is reported. THE EMPTY GROUP IS BUILT AND STEPPED RATHER THAN REFUSED, as the docstring promises: {'base':[p],'encoder':[]}, {'base':[p]} with the key absent, and {'base':[],'encoder':[p]} all build, all record params.base/params.encoder honestly, and maybe_step steps over them without torch's 'optimizer got an empty parameter list'.

THE LOSS FALLS, AND I SAY PLAINLY WHAT THE BATCH WAS. Two arms, both driven only through opt.scaled_backward / opt.maybe_step / opt.lr_at, batch = 16 windows of 32 tokens. FRESH BATCH EVERY STEP (a 16-window slice walked through the stream, wrapping): cross-entropy at steps 0,50,100,200,300,500,700,900,1100,1175 = 8.3329, 4.8951, 4.9833, 5.6350, 4.5546, 3.4835, 2.6504, 3.8330, 2.4268, 2.2485 nats/token = 6.6324 -> 1.8264 bits/byte. The stream is 2068 windows, so 1200 steps x 16 windows is ~9 passes over one 66k-token synthetic corpus: the fall is real descent plus memorisation of a small corpus, and there is NO held-out number in this run. FIXED BATCH (the same 16 windows for all 300 steps): 8.3329 -> 0.0085, which is overfitting one batch and is a smoke test, not a result -- stated here because the recorded r2 run reported its 0.144 without that distinction being the headline. In both arms all_stepped=True, opt.step == opt.backward == the step count, opt.lr.writes.base == opt.lr.writes.encoder == opt.step, opt.encoder_steps_here == 0 (the Q-OPT-6 regression counter), and opt.counters() did not raise its accumulation invariant. The rate came back as a RETURN VALUE on every call (StepOutcome.lr), never as a local: lr[step1]=1.9417e-05, lr[step206]=2e-3 (peak), lr[step1200]=9.4921e-04.

THE FABRIC'S PARAMETERS DO MOVE UNDER THE REAL OPTIMIZER -- and the real number is NOT the recorded one. Every tensor Population.parameters() returns is inside the base AdamW (20 fabric tensors of the 48 in the group, verified by id()). With the fabric used the way src/fabric/api.py::forward would use it -- h + h @ A[0] @ B[0] added to the residual stream before LM.decode, the LoRA/expert shape -- and OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY at its shipped 0.0: max|B_before-B_after| = 0.0055426 with B first moving on step 1 (grad|B|max = 4.8799e-03 on the first backward), max|A_before-A_after| = 0.0053789 with A first moving on step 2 (grad|A|max = 0.0 on the first backward, because B is zero-init, then nonzero once B leaves zero). Over the 1200-step run: A moved 0.19535, B moved 0.17244. So the mechanism both goals rest on is live under the real optimizer. THE OTHER 17 FABRIC TENSORS NEVER MOVE (halt_b, eemb, edec, q_route, hproj, halt_key, norm, nov_proj): their .grad is None on every step, because only the unbuilt router reads them. That is FAB.forward being a stub, not OPT.

THE RECORDED 0.000529 IS NOT LEARNING, IT IS WEIGHT DECAY, AND THE MEASUREMENT IT CERTIFIES IS VOID. .rework/audits/r2_sweep_full.json's end_to_end record states 'max|Population.A_before - Population.A_after| = 0.000529 > 0, confirming the expert tensors genuinely moved under gradient descent'. src/fabric/api.py::build draws A uniform(-1/sqrt(d_model), +) and leaves B at ZERO ('A is drawn, B stays ZERO'), and the stand-in that run used reaches A and B ONLY through their product: (h_mean @ A[0] @ B[0]).pow(2).mean(). At B=0 that term is 0 and BOTH gradients are identically 0 -- d/dA = grad_out @ B^T = 0 and d/dB = (hA)^T @ grad_out = 0 because grad_out = 2(hAB)/N = 0. I re-ran that exact configuration (LM_WIDTH=32, batch 8, 30 steps, torch.optim.AdamW(params, lr=1e-2)) and measured: grad|A|max = 0.0, grad|B|max = 0.0, fab_term = 0.0 on step 0; max|A_before-A_after| = 0.000529483, matching the record to four figures; and A_after/A_before is a CONSTANT 0.9970036-0.9970042 across every one of the 8192 entries, against the predicted decoupled-decay ratio (1 - lr*wd)^30 = 0.9970043 for torch's AdamW DEFAULT weight_decay=0.01 -- which that line never set. B moved 0.0. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS PACKAGE IS THE INVERSE OF WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE: with the REAL OPT, whose OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY defaults to 0.0, the same term moves A by EXACTLY 0.0, so a reader comparing the two runs would read the real optimizer as the regression. It is not: the stand-in was stationary at init in both, and only the old run's unrequested decay made it look otherwise. Filed against fabric/api.py::build because the zero-init of B is what makes any product-only objective stationary; it is NOT a defect in src/opt/api.py. The open question it leaves is for FAB: whether the real forward reaches A and B other than through their product (see UNFINISHED).

ACCUMULATION AT OPT_ACCUM=4: THE GATE, THE SCALING AND THE not_due REPORTS ALL HOLD. Over 24 consecutive calls the optimizer stepped on calls 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23 -- exactly once per 4 backwards -- and maybe_step returned stepped=False on the other 18, with opt.step.not_due = 18, opt.step = 6, opt.backward = 24. THE GRADIENT IS SCALED, CHECKED AGAINST A TRUE FULL-BATCH GRADIENT AND NOT AGAINST A COUNTER: four micro-batches of 4 windows through opt.scaled_backward, against ONE plain .backward() over the concatenated 16-window batch on an identically-seeded fresh model, gave max|g_accum - g_single| = 1.21e-08 over all 48 base tensors and sum|g_accum|/sum|g_single| = 0.99999999 -- 1.0, not 4.0. So the effective batch is right rather than the learning signal being 4x, which is the failure mode scaled_backward's docstring names. The horizon moved with it: run_windows=2068 with d_effective_batch_windows=4 gave Steps(517) and warmup min(1000, 517//10) = 51. At OPT_BATCH_WINDOWS=4 OPT_ACCUM=2 through the same real loop: d_effective_batch_windows=8, run_steps=258, one step per 2 flushes, and counters() printed 'opt.backward=12  opt.step=6  accum=2  batch_windows=4  d_effective_batch_windows=8' without raising.

GRAD CLIP CLIPS, AND REPORTS BOTH OF ITS TWO ARMED STATES. I read the norm the optimizer ACTUALLY STEPPED ON by registering a step_pre_hook on st.base, which fires after maybe_step's clip and before st.base.step(), so it sees the post-clip gradient without touching src/. At OPT_GRAD_CLIP=1.0 with the loss amplified 100x, over 10 steps: pre-clip norms recorded on st.grad_norms were 76.33-83.76 and every post-clip norm the optimizer saw was 1.0000 -- post == min(pre, clip) to within 1e-4 on all 10 steps; opt.clip.applied = 10, opt.clip.armed_no_clip = 0, gate 'opt.clip.applied: FIRED (10 vs max-norm 1.0)'. The rendered quantiles are the PRE-clip norms (p50=79.06, p99=83.76), which is what the docstring promises -- an instrument that measured its own remedy would have printed 1.0. At OPT_GRAD_CLIP=1e6 with no amplification: opt.clip.applied = 0, opt.clip.armed_no_clip = 10, and the gate reads 'armed, did not fire (0 vs max-norm 1000000.0) -- armed and NOTHING exceeded the norm', which is the correct third statement. At the shipped 0.0 both gates render UNREACHABLE with the Q-OPT-3 sentence, not 'armed, did not fire'.

DETERMINISM HOLDS ON BOTH HALVES, THROUGH THE REAL OPT, AND OPT DOES NOT DEFEAT D12. Six fresh processes, 40 real optimizer steps each, digest over the full loss sequence and over the 48 base tensors' sums. At LM_DROPOUT=0.0: RUN_SEED=0 twice -> LOSS_DIGEST 1479b596b7c2a80f and PARAM_DIGEST bac1bbf530de139f BOTH times; RUN_SEED=1 -> a1ad171ea3abad7d / cf850ec7bb8bf83e, different. At LM_DROPOUT=0.2, where the transformer's dropout draws from torch's process-global generator and D12 is the only thing seeding it: RUN_SEED=0 twice -> 616a12d93727e3ad / 315179afaa733b43 BOTH times; RUN_SEED=1 -> b38f06ed77626dc9 / c0d40088452609b0, different. torch.initial_seed() after process_setup was 3734753547471956429 for seed 0 in both processes and 1763737848520504121 for seed 1, i.e. derived from RUN_SEED and not from OS entropy. src/opt/api.py contains no RNG of any kind (no torch.rand, no Generator, no rng_for), and the returned schedule was identical across seeds (lr at step 40 = 3.980582524e-04 in all six runs), which is the right answer -- the schedule is seed-independent by construction.

findings.detail: THE RESTART DETECTOR IS BLINDED BY THE ENVELOPE, AND I CAN NOW PUT A NUMBER ON HOW MUCH. ALREADY FILED by .rework/audits/v_opt_gates.json and .rework/audits/v_opt_contract.json; this is independent runtime confirmation plus the missing quantity. Detection requires `lr > 1.5*st.lr_prev AND lr > 0.5*opt.lr`, while the shipped OPT_LR_DECAY=1.0 envelope drives successive cycle peaks down. Holding restart_amp at 1.0 (no damping at all, so this is the CEILING on detection) over a 2068-step horizon at OPT_LR_WARMUP=20, restarts in the run vs restarts the detector can ever see: wavelength=1200 -> 1 of 1; 700 -> 1 of 2; 520 -> 2 of 3; 400 -> 2 of 4; 300 -> 3 of 6; 210 -> 5 of 10. At OPT_LR_DECAY=0.0 every one is detected (1/1, 2/2, 3/3, 4/4, 6/6, 10/10), so the blinding is exactly the interaction of the two shipped defaults. Measured cycle peaks at wavelength=520: 0.002, 0.00172175, 0.00105, 0.00037825 against a 0.5*lr bar of 0.001. DRIVEN LIVE with a never-improving Reading(2.5, seed_count=3) for 2068 steps: only 2 restarts detected (steps 532 and 1044), 1 damped, restart_amp 1.0 -> 0.5, and the fourth cycle then peaks at 0.00019858 -- under the detector's own bar, so the damping switches itself off after ONE click. counters() prints 'Gate opt.lr.restarts: FIRED (2 vs 4 cycles fitted)', which reads as a measurement of a mechanism that fired twice, not as an instrument that cannot see the other two. This matters for GOAL A specifically: the undetectable restarts are the LATE ones, which is where the package's own docstring puts the failure it exists to fix.

AT OPT_LR_SCHED=none THE SCHED GATE PRINTS 'armed, did not fire' FOR A MECHANISM THAT CANNOT FIRE, WITH ITS OWN REASON SAYING SO IN THE SAME LINE. ALREADY FILED by .rework/audits/v_opt_contract.json and .rework/audits/v_opt_gates.json; recorded here because I hit it while driving the Goal-A ablation and the printed line is worth having verbatim. The Gate is constructed with a hard-coded `reachable=True`, so a 40-step real run at OPT_LR_SCHED=none renders: 'Gate opt.lr.sched: armed, did not fire (none vs cosine) -- OPT_LR_SCHED=none: warmup, wavelength, floor, restarts, damping, envelope and re-warm are ALL structurally unreachable, which is what makes this an ablation rather than an arm'. spine/gate.py::Gate.line reserves 'armed, did not fire' for fired=False AND reachable=True, and the sentence printed after it asserts unreachability -- one line making both statements. THE ABLATION ITSELF TRAINS CORRECTLY, which is the part that matters for Goal A and is why I class this as a reporting defect and not a training one: the rate set was exactly {0.002} on every one of 40 steps, both optimizers' param groups carried 0.002, cross-entropy fell 8.3329 -> 4.8743, and opt.lr.in_warmup / damped_this_step / shift_warm_applied / envelope_applied were all 0. ISSUES P1-H15 (the `_lrv` NameError on the first flush at LR_SCHED=none) is dead.

THE not_due BRANCH RETURNS 0.0 AS 'THE RATE THE OPTIMIZER IS CURRENTLY AT' WHILE THE OPTIMIZER IS AT THE PEAK. ALREADY FILED by .rework/audits/v_opt_contract.json; the measurement it lacked is the live group value at that instant. build() constructs both AdamW instances with lr=opt.lr, so at OPT_ACCUM=4 the first three calls of a run measure: call 0/1/2 stepped=False, returned lr=0, LIVE st.base.param_groups[0]['lr']=0.002; call 3 stepped=True, returned lr=8e-05, live 8e-05; calls 4/5 stepped=False, returned 8e-05, live 8e-05. So the branch's own comment ('THE RATE THE OPTIMIZER IS CURRENTLY AT, not a fresh one: no step was taken, so nothing rewrote the param groups') is false for exactly the accum-1 calls at the start of a run, and in the direction that hands FAB.own_lr_scale a zero rate. It cannot occur at the shipped OPT_ACCUM=1, where every call steps.

THE WARMUP RAMP IS ONE STEP SHORT AND NEVER EMITS ITS FIRST RUNG. ALREADY FILED by .rework/audits/v_opt_units.json; confirmed at runtime and reported here only for the numbers. maybe_step advances st.opt_step BEFORE pricing, so the first priced step is 1, while _schedule prices warmup as `lr * (step + 1) / w`, which assumes a 0-based step. At OPT_LR_WARMUP=20, peak 2e-3, the rates lr_at actually returns are: step 1 -> 0.0002 (0.100 of peak), step 2 -> 0.0003, ..., step 18 -> 0.0019 (0.950), step 19 -> 0.002 (1.000 of peak), step 20 -> 0.002. So peak is reached at step 19 of a warmup declared 20 long, the ramp has 19 rungs not 20, and the lowest rung -- lr_at(Steps(0)) = 0.0001 -- is a step maybe_step never prices. At the shipped OPT_LR_WARMUP=1000 the error is 0.1% of the warmup and moves no recorded result.

THE PROPERTY THE DOCSTRING SINGLES OUT HOLDS AT EVERY RESTART COUNT I COULD FIT. 'The schedule's minimum over a whole run equals lr * lr_min_frac at EVERY restart count, single-cycle included': over the full 2068-step horizon at OPT_LR_WARMUP=20 and the shipped lr_min_frac=0.05, lr_decay=1.0, lr_restarts=on, min(lr over the run) = 0.0001 = 2e-3 * 0.05 EXACTLY at n_cycles = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 11 (wavelengths 0, 1200, 700, 520, 400, 300, 210), with max = 0.002 in every case, so the final `cyc = max(min_frac, cyc)` clamp is doing the work the P4 note claims for it. Separately, 'at exactly one fitted cycle the schedule is bit-identical to lr_restarts=off' holds at the 0 sentinel: 2000 rates compared, max abs diff 0.0, lists equal. (v_opt_contract.json files that same sentence as FALSE at explicitly-set wavelengths; my check covers only the sentinel path, so the two are not in conflict.) The shift re-warm is an ATTENUATION and never a raise: with OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM=30 and a shift stamped at step 1195, lr(1195+k)/lr_unshifted was <= 1.0 at every offset and floored at lr*lr_min_frac rather than diving under it.

THE PLAN 3.8 SEED-COUNT REFUSAL IS REAL AND IT FIRES WHERE IT IS SUPPOSED TO. Driving 2068 steps with Reading(value=2.5, seed_count=1) -- a cycle that never pays, on n=1 -- gave opt.restart.detected=2, opt.restart.damped=0, opt.restart.damp_refused_n1=1, restart_amp still 1.0: the refusal is counted, not damped quietly. (One refusal for two detections is correct: at the FIRST restart st.cycle_best is None so `paid` is True and no verdict is attempted.) At seed_count=3 the same drive gives detected=2, damped=1, restart_amp 1.0 -> 0.5. A BARE FLOAT best_bpb=2.5 raises ValueError('OPT.maybe_step: best_bpb=2.5 carries no seed count...') -- but only at the first step where a restart is DETECTED (step 532 here), never before, because _reading is called inside `if restart:`. On a single-cycle run at the shipped defaults the guard can never fire at all.

unfinished.detail: The hypothesis this package is the leading candidate for is about steps 6,000-48,000 on held-out text. My longest run was 1,200 optimizer steps on CPU, on a 66k-token synthetic corpus it re-passes about nine times, with no held-out split evaluated: src/eval/api.py's entry points are stubs (8 NotImplementedError), so there is no bits/byte reading in this tree to take. Everything I report about the schedule is therefore about the INSTRUMENT being sound, not about the hypothesis being right. Nothing I ran can distinguish 'the schedule is correct' from 'the schedule is correct and still the wrong schedule'.

unfinished.title: Whether the fabric's A and B can move under the REAL router is still open, and the zero-init question lands on FAB
unfinished.detail: I had to wire the population into the loss by hand. My 'residual' stand-in (h + h @ A[0] @ B[0] before LM.decode) is the LoRA/expert shape and gives B a gradient on step 1 and A one on step 2, which is how a zero-init B is SUPPOSED to come alive. The recorded r2 stand-in ((h_mean @ A[0] @ B[0])^2) is stationary at init and gives neither a gradient ever. Both are guesses at what forward will do. THE THING TO CHECK WHEN forward EXISTS: any objective that reaches A and B only through their product AB, with no other route to either and no symmetry-breaking outside the gradient, leaves the whole expert pool frozen at its initialisation for the entire run while every counter and every loss curve looks healthy -- which is precisely the 'both goals' central mechanism, inert, with the arithmetic intact' failure src/fabric/api.py::Population.__init__ already has a paragraph about. src/fabric/api.py::manage and ::grow_check (replication with mutation) are the other candidate symmetry-breakers and are also stubs.

I drove the first and third directly, in that order, which is what compose declares; the middle row could not run. So OPT's own st.n_backward and the RunClock's Backwards clock have never been compared against each other, and ISSUES P3-H29 (55 optimizer steps where 13 were due) is only dead on OPT's side of that join.

That is the correct answer today and an untested path tomorrow: nothing has ever exercised st.encoder.step(), its moments, or its half of state_dict/load_state under a real gradient.
